content: 1. Rifapentine reduces the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of vonoprazan by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Vonoprazan decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of rilpivirine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. The combination is contraindicated. 3. Vonoprazan increases the plasma concentration and effect of sirolimus by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so care should be taken with drugs that are sensitive CYP3A substrates. 4. Sotorasib reduces the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of vonoprazan by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. St. John’s Wort decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of vonoprazan by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. Vonoprazan increases the plasma concentration and effect of tacrolimus by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so care should be taken with drugs that are sensitive CYP3A substrates. 7. Vonoprazan increases the plasma concentration and effect of theophylline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so care should be taken with drugs that are sensitive CYP3A substrates. 8. Vonoprazan increases the plasma concentration and effect of triazolam by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, so care should be taken with drugs that are sensitive CYP3A substrates. 9. Vonoprazan has been associated with blood and lymphatic system disorders, including thrombocytopenia. Immune system disorders such as anaphylactic shock have also been reported. 10. Infections caused by Clostridioides difficile have been observed, particularly when vonoprazan is used in combination with antibacterial agents. 11. Laboratory abnormalities such as hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, and vitamin B12 deficiency have been reported. 12. Hepatobiliary disorders, including hepatic injury, hepatic failure, and jaundice, have been associated with vonoprazan use. 13. Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders, such as drug eruptions, erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), have been reported. 14. Vonoprazan is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to the drug or its components. 15. Products containing rilpivirine are contraindicated with vonoprazan due to the inhibition of gastric pH by vonoprazan, which reduces rilpivirine absorption. 16. The combination of vonoprazan with clarithromycin and amoxicillin is contraindicated in certain cases. Refer to specific drug monographs for details. 17. Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis has been reported with vonoprazan use. If suspected, the drug should be discontinued, and the patient should be evaluated. 18. Severe cutaneous adverse reactions, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), have been reported. The drug should be discontinued at the first signs of these reactions or other hypersensitivity symptoms, and further evaluation should be considered. 19. Long-term use of acid-suppressing drugs, including vonoprazan, may lead to malabsorption of vitamin B12 due to hypoor achlorhydria. Postmarketing reports have noted vitamin B12 deficiency with vonoprazan use. Further evaluation should be considered if clinical symptoms consistent with vitamin B12 deficiency are observed. 20. Available pharmacovigilance data on vonoprazan use during pregnancy are insufficient to assess the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Pregnancies should be reported to Phathom Pharmaceuticals, Inc., via their adverse event reporting line. 21. There is no data on the presence of vonoprazan in human breast milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. However, vonoprazan and its metabolites are present in rat milk, and liver injury has been observed in offspring of pregnant and lactating rats exposed to vonoprazan at doses approximating or exceeding the maximum recommended human dose. 22. Vonoprazan is a potassium-competitive acid blocker (PCAB) that suppresses both basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion by inhibiting the H+/K+-ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of gastric parietal cells. This enzyme is considered the acid (proton) pump of the parietal cell, making vonoprazan a type of gastric proton-pump inhibitor that blocks the final step of acid production. 23. Unlike traditional proton-pump inhibitors, vonoprazan does not require activation by acid and may selectively concentrate in parietal cells in both resting and stimulated states. It binds to active proton pumps in a noncovalent and reversible manner. 24. Vonoprazan is 85-88% protein-bound and is metabolized into inactive metabolites via multiple pathways involving cytochrome P450 (CYP) isoforms (CYP3A4/5, CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, and CYP2D6) as well as sulfoand glucuronosyl-transferases. 25. CYP2C19 polymorphisms have been evaluated in clinical studies, and no significant differences in vonoprazan pharmacokinetics were observed based on CYP2C19 metabolizer status. 26. Vonoprazan can be taken with or without food. Tablets should be swallowed whole and not chewed or crushed.
